A complete guide for small businesses

[

Get started

](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en/guides/how-to-win-local-advertising#6fTzXwbrZfT4B1l1XSpiIq)

![TT CAFE2 0697 07](https://lf-tt4b.tiktokcdn.com/obj/i18nblog/tt4b_cms/en-US/tipdilz7wysq-5LFnDheSHQBd9LthYifEEw.jpg "TT CAFE2 0697 07")

GLOSSARY

## Local advertising terms

This page explains core local advertising concepts and TikTok targeting options for nearby customer reach.

*   • **Local advertising**: Reaching people in your area most likely to visit, call, or order locally.
*   • **Location targeting**: Setting ads to specific regions so they reach the right local audience efficiently.
*   • **DMA regions (Designated Market Areas)**: U.S. media regions covering groups of counties with similar TV and media content.
*   • **Smart+ campaigns**: TikTok campaigns that automatically adjust bidding, placements, audiences, and creatives for performance.

### What is local advertising?

Local advertising is about showing up where it matters most, in your own neighborhood. Instead of trying to compete everywhere, you focus on the people most likely to walk through your door, call for your services, or order in your delivery zone. Local ads connect you with nearby customers through digital tools, community channels, and even classic media. The goal is simple: help people discover you the moment they need you.

  

For example, a neighborhood café might run short-form video ads highlighting its seasonal drinks, showing content to local consumers. A family-owned gym could use location targeting to reach new residents in the area with a free trial offer. Local service providers, like a plumber or home repair business, might promote ads during evening hours when people are most likely to need help fast. Even community staples like bookstores or boutiques can use event-based advertising to invite people to in-store workshops, sales, or launches.

  

These local advertising approaches make your business feel visible, approachable, and present in daily community life, no matter what channel you use.

#### Get started today

[Sign up](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en/guides/how-to-win-local-advertising#6ZaQrxi4daN4Q2WlDYCbfq) [Log in](https://ads.tiktok.com/i18n/login)

### Why local advertising matters

When people search for something nearby, they usually want it now. That urgency creates a huge opportunity for small businesses to step in at the right time and drive your business forward, whether that means foot traffic, conversations, or direct sales.

  

Local ads also build confidence. People trust businesses that feel connected to their community, and showing up with relevant, local messaging proves you understand what they need.

  

The shift to mobile has made this even more important. Most people now turn to their phones first to find what they need, whether that is a late-night meal, a last-minute gift, or a service close to home. Local searches happen in the moment, often when people are ready to take action. If your business is not visible when someone nearby is scrolling or searching, you miss out on customers who are ready to decide.

  

Competition is often lighter at the neighborhood level, giving you a chance to stand out without matching the budgets of larger companies. By showing up with simple, clear, and relevant ads, you can become the first choice in your community.

# TikTok for Small Business: 7 Content Ideas

Learn how small businesses use TikTok to start converting views to sales, with advice from founders and marketers who’ve done it successfully.

![](https://www.gravatar.com/avatar/d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e?s=200&d=404)

[by Lauren Strapagiel](https://www.shopify.com/blog/authors/lauren-strapagiel)Dec 18, 2025 • 12 min read

![purple cellphone laying down pointed toward top right corner with small beam of light emanating from screen with five cubes floating in light all in front of a orange pink red purple background](https://cdn.shopify.com/b/shopify-brochure2-assets/0b79a276070d3be542ee38b9068a2e4a.jpg?originalWidth=1848&originalHeight=782)

In the digital age, [TikTok marketing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/tiktok-marketing) has quickly become one of the best ways to showcase a variety of businesses. If you [know your audience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/know-your-audience) is part of the approximately [two billion active users](https://www.statista.com/statistics/272014/global-social-networks-ranked-by-number-of-users/) worldwide, it’s worth considering as part of your [marketing strategy](https://www.shopify.com/blog/marketing-strategies).

According to [_The Washington Post_](https://www.washingtonpost.com/wellness/interactive/2025/tiktok-addiction-algorithm-scrolling-mental-health/), “light users” spend an average of 30 minutes a day on the app, while “power users” spend an average of four hours or more per day. TikTok is known for memes, dance challenges, and viral moments, and it’s attracted top brands and small businesses for its extensive reach. In fact, you’d be hard-pressed to find top sellers who aren’t at least experimenting with content on the app.

As with any social platform, TikTok has its unique quirks, filters, and [trends](https://www.shopify.com/blog/tiktok-trends) to navigate.

But fear not—this article provides help from small-business TikTok pros and ideas to get started. And if you’re already on TikTok, you might pick up some inspiration.

## Why small businesses should be posting on TikTok

TikTok is a powerful tool for building [brand awareness](https://www.shopify.com/blog/brand-awareness) beyond your existing audience. The app’s homepage, known as the For You page, or FYP, serves users a never-ending stream of content its [sophisticated algorithm](https://www.shopify.com/blog/tiktok-algorithm) determines they’ll like. This means potential [high value customers](https://www.shopify.com/blog/high-value-customer) can find your videos without directly seeking out your brand.

TikTok primes users to discover new brands directly in the app. According to [Capital One research](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/tiktok-shopping-statistics/), “49% of users say that TikTok creators inspire them to explore the products and brands they promote.” Additionally, it notes that Americans spend an estimated $32 million per day on the app. This unique take on discoverability has allowed accounts of all sizes to become overnight viral sensations.

Erin Dubs, owner of fitness clothing brand [Azur Fit](https://azurfit.com/), has amassed 120,000 followers on her [TikTok account](http://tiktok.com/@erinndubs).

“TikTok is not something that can be ignored,” Erin says. “It definitely gives you a step up if you do have it.”

She says that when she has a popular TikTok post, the effect is immediate: “When that happens, there’s consistently always 300 people on the website all day long. It’ll bring in 60,000 views over the course of just a few days.”

The first time Erin went viral on TikTok, her inventory was wiped out.

Even TikToks with smaller view counts are valuable, she says, because they still [drive traffic to her website](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-increase-website-traffic) and Instagram. Other founders have seen similar results, using [TikTok for business](https://www.shopify.com/blog/tiktok-for-business) as a way to bring awareness to their shops.

“It’s eyes on your website, and it works really well,” Erin says.” Sometimes I just need that reminder, like, ‘Oh yeah, make a TikTok today.’”

## Best practices for using TikTok for your small business

Learning [how to use TikTok](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-use-tiktok) can help you find [viral success](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-go-viral-on-tiktok) and connect with a [target audience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/target-audience) that’s obsessed with your product.
